q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT S1.bar, S2.bar FROM serves AS S1 LEFT JOIN serves AS S2 ON S1.beer = S2.beer

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT S1.bar, S2.bar FROM serves AS S1 LEFT JOIN serves AS S2 ON S1.beer = S2.beer

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 checks for bars that serve a unique beer (no other bar serves this beer) and another bar that does not serve this beer, while Q2 lists all pairs of bars that serve the same beer.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have two bars, 'Bar A' and 'Bar B', where 'Bar A' serves a unique beer 'Beer X' that 'Bar B' does not serve, and 'Bar B' serves another beer 'Beer Y' that 'Bar A' also serves.
